faq.q: Which cursive signature style is the most readable?
faq.a: Bold Cursive. Its strokes are thicker, every letter comes from one widely supported Unicode range, and it stays legible at small sizes such as an Instagram bio or an email footer. Lighter script styles look more elegant but lose detail on small screens.

faq.q: Can I use a Unicode cursive signature on legal documents?
faq.a: No. A copy-and-paste cursive signature is decorative text, not a legal signature. For contracts and forms, use the platform's own e-signature tool or sign by hand. Use the cursive version for profiles, captions, email sign-offs and creative projects.

faq.q: Should my signature include my full name?
faq.a: Only if it fits. First name alone, or first name plus last initial, reads better in bios and captions than a long full name. For a personal brand or a business, the full name gives search engines and readers more to work with.

faq.q: Do decorative symbols around a signature cause display problems?
faq.a: They can. Symbols such as ꧁ and ꧂ come from scripts that not every device includes, so some viewers may see boxes. Plain hearts (♡) and stars (★) are safer. If in doubt, copy the signature without symbols and test it on a second phone.
